raw_response:
I've been working this land in Quzhou my whole life, same as my father before me. I don't need to think hard about what to grow — here, you grow wheat in the cold months and corn in the hot months. That's what the land is for, that's what the market takes, and that's what I know. I have about 8 mu of flat field. I'll plant wheat come October and corn as soon as the wheat is off in June. Same rotation I've done for forty years.

For seeds, I go to the village store and buy what the man there tells me is good this year — always the improved kind, not the old seeds, because the yields are better. For wheat I'll use something like Jimai or Kenong, whatever he has. For corn, Zhengdan 958 or something similar. My neighbors use these and they do well.

Fertilizer — I put down a good base when planting and top-dress the wheat in spring. I don't weigh things precisely; I know by habit roughly how much a bag covers. I use compound fertilizer plus urea. Corn gets more nitrogen because it needs it.

Water — we irrigate here, we have to. For wheat I water three times: before winter sets in, then when it joints, then before heading. Corn I water twice. The well is shared and it costs money, so I don't waste.

For spraying, wheat gets two rounds — once for weeds, once before harvest for aphids and rust. Corn just needs one round usually.

At 70, the heavy tillage I hire someone with a machine for. Rotary tilling is standard here now.
